The results of this work suggest that many of the Inflation Reduction Act's clean energy initiatives, that have since been repealed, are effective near-term solutions to reduce exposure to fossil fuel price and mitigate future financial penalties associated with the rising social cost of carbon.
tldr: This paper analyzes US energy system emissions and costs using an open-source model, focusing on fossil fuel price volatility and methane leakage.
motivation: The US is unlikely to meet its 2030 Paris Agreement target, and the paper aims to identify effective near-term abatement strategies.
method: The authors extend the PyPSA-USA energy system model for multi-sector analysis and apply global sensitivity analysis to evaluate drivers of costs and emissions.
result: Fossil fuel price volatility dominates marginal costs, while system climate impact is highly sensitive to fugitive methane leakage rates and global warming potential assumptions.
conclusion: Addressing upstream methane leaks and promoting demand-side electrification are effective near-term solutions to reduce emissions and fossil fuel exposure.

title: Verification And Performance Assessment Of NuDEAL, A GPU-Accelerated Deterministic Transport Framework On Unstructured Meshes
authors: Kyung Min Kim, Jaeuk Im, Han Gyu Lee, Yeon Sang Jung
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-fidelity neutronic analyses of advanced reactors require deterministic transport solvers capable of handling complex unstructured geometries while maintaining computational efficiency. This work presents the development and verification of three GPU-accelerated deterministic solvers implemented within a unified framework, Neutronics using Deterministic Finite Element Algorithm (NuDEAL): the planar Method of Characteristics coupled with the Hybrid Finite Element Method (MOC/HFEM), the Discontinuous Galerkin Method of Characteristics (DGMOC), and the Discontinuous Finite Element discrete ordinate method (DFEM-SN). These solvers provide complementary capabilities for consistently solving the multigroup transport equation and can be selectively employed to balance accuracy, computational cost, and memory requirements for a given problem. All methods emphasize efficient GPU execution by leveraging memory alignment, compressed-flux storage, and sequential azimuthal sweeps. The solvers are validated on the C5G7 benchmark and applied to advanced reactor problems, including the ABTR, Empire microreactor, and MSRE. DFEM-SN achieved the highest accuracy, with eigenvalue errors below 50 pcm, while MOC/HFEM and DGMOC provided superior efficiency, with single-GPU runtimes comparable to those of large CPU clusters. The results demonstrate that deterministic GPU solvers on unstructured meshes can deliver both accuracy and scalability, enabling practical whole-core simulations for heterogeneous advanced reactors. The unified NuDEAL framework establishes a foundation for future extensions toward transient and multiphysics analyses on large-scale GPU architectures.
tldr: This paper presents a GPU-accelerated deterministic transport framework for neutronic analysis of advanced nuclear reactors.
motivation: High-fidelity neutronic analyses of advanced reactors require efficient deterministic transport solvers on unstructured meshes.
method: Three GPU-accelerated solvers (MOC/HFEM, DGMOC, DFEM-SN) are implemented in the NuDEAL framework, leveraging memory alignment and compressed-flux storage.
result: DFEM-SN achieves eigenvalue errors below 50 pcm, while MOC/HFEM and DGMOC offer single-GPU runtimes comparable to large CPU clusters.
conclusion: The NuDEAL framework enables accurate and scalable whole-core simulations for heterogeneous advanced reactors on GPU architectures.

title: Memory Device For Photons By Exploiting Brillouin Interactions In Nanowires
authors: Hashem Zoubi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Memory devices for single photons are notable components for quantum information processing and quantum communications. The present study investigates the possibility of achieving storage of light at the level of single photons inside nanofibers by exploiting stimulated Brillouin scattering. We present first the standard approach using a coherent buffer in a nanoscale waveguide by transferring the optical signal coherently to an acoustic wave, and that can be extracted by the reverse process. The life time of the acoustic wave put limitation on the applicability of such approach for single photon signals. We introduce a configuration for achieving a slow signal at the level of single photons without gain or loss. The process utilizes photon-phonon Brillouin interactions involving two counter propagating pump fields. The photon storage is achieved through time delay of significantly slow signal inside nanowires. We address the condition for getting negligible influence due to the scattering off thermal phonons.
tldr: Analysis failed

title: Atomic Decomposition Of Anisotropic Herz-Amalgam Spaces And Boundedness Of Sublinear Operators
authors: Mehvish Sultan, Amjad Husssain, Babar Sultan, Tariq Mahmood
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we introduce the idea of anisotropic Herz-Amalgam spaces. Then we find the atomic decomposition in these spaces. As an application, in these spaces, we demonstrate the boundedness of certain sublinear operators.
tldr: This paper introduces anisotropic Herz-Amalgam spaces and provides atomic decomposition and boundedness results for sublinear operators.
motivation: To extend the theory of Herz-Amalgam spaces to anisotropic settings, enabling analysis of function spaces with different scaling properties.
method: The authors define anisotropic Herz-Amalgam spaces using a dilation matrix and prove atomic decomposition via covering arguments and discrete characterizations.
result: Atomic decomposition is established for these spaces, and boundedness of certain sublinear operators is demonstrated.
conclusion: The work contributes to harmonic analysis and function space theory but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Restatement Of Fixed Point Existence: From Banach To Singh Contractions
authors: Zouaoui Bekri Nicola Fabiano
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a reformulation of classical existence and uniqueness results for second-order boundary value problems (BVPs). For Singh contractions, we allow [MATH] to satisfy the condition, providing greater flexibility. Examples illustrate the applicability of all results. The work highlights the utility of generalized contractions in differential equations, particularly when the Banach contraction principle fails.
tldr: This paper reformulates fixed point existence results for second-order boundary value problems using Singh contractions, a generalization of Banach contractions.
motivation: To provide a more flexible condition for proving existence and uniqueness of solutions to boundary value problems when the Banach contraction principle fails.
method: The authors restate classical fixed point theorems and extend them to Singh contractions, allowing a weaker contractive condition, and provide illustrative examples.
result: The reformulation yields existence and uniqueness results for second-order BVPs under generalized contractions, with examples demonstrating applicability.
conclusion: Generalized contractions like Singh contractions are useful tools in differential equations, especially when standard Banach contractions are not applicable.

title: Null Cartan Normal Helices In Minkowski Space-Time
authors: Umut Selvi Derya Sa\u{g}lam
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A complete theory of null Cartan normal helices in Minkowski space-time [MATH] is developed. Two algebraic conditions, obtained by successive differentiation of the helix invariant along a unit [MATH]-constant normal field, fully characterize null Cartan helices; the quadratic condition yields two mutually orthogonal helix axes in the Lorentzian metric. Special field types are analyzed and null Cartan cubics are shown to be normal helices. On a timelike hypersurface, a Darboux frame with six curvature functions is constructed from first principles, the normal isophotic condition is shown to reduce to a linear first-order ODE, and the existence of normal silhouettes in [MATH] is established.
tldr: This paper develops a complete theory of null Cartan normal helices in Minkowski space-time, focusing on differential geometry of curves and surfaces.
motivation: To characterize null Cartan helices in Lorentzian geometry and extend the theory to timelike hypersurfaces with Darboux frames.
method: Successive differentiation of the helix invariant along a unit constant normal field yields algebraic conditions; a Darboux frame with six curvature functions is constructed from first principles.
result: Two algebraic conditions fully characterize null Cartan helices, yielding two orthogonal helix axes; null Cartan cubics are shown to be normal helices; normal silhouettes exist in Minkowski space.
conclusion: The paper provides a complete geometric characterization of null Cartan normal helices, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: $\lambda_\infty$: A New Mathematical Constant From The Spectral Theory Of The Prime Lcm Matrix
authors: Alessandro Munari
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a new mathematical constant [MATH] (OEIS A396695), defined as the unique solution in [MATH] of [MATH]. This equation arises as the [MATH] limit of the secular equation of rank-[MATH] truncations of the infinite prime LCM matrix [MATH], where [MATH]. Viewed as a compact self-adjoint operator on [MATH], [MATH] has spectral radius [MATH] (Theorem 5.4). The corresponding integer LCM matrix satisfies [MATH] (Theorem 5.8), a prime-indexed counterpart to [MATH] for the integer divisor matrix. We prove that [MATH] is real-analytic, strictly decreasing and strictly convex on [MATH], ensuring existence and uniqueness of [MATH]. We compute 500 decimal digits of [MATH], certified by rigorous error bounds and independently verified by six computational runs, including a fully independent recomputation (Run E, PARI-GP) and a machine-verifiable Arb interval certificate (Run F) covering 505 digits. Extensive PSLQ and LLL searches find no minimal polynomial of degree [MATH] satisfied by [MATH] (at 560 decimal digits), and no integer relation against catalogs of up to 31 classical constants. motivation: The authors aim to introduce and characterize a new constant arising from the spectral properties of a matrix related to prime numbers.
method: The constant is defined as the unique solution to an equation derived from the secular equation of truncations of the infinite prime LCM matrix, analyzed using real analysis and computational methods.
result: The constant is proven to be real-analytic, strictly decreasing, and strictly convex; 500 decimal digits are computed with rigorous error bounds.
conclusion: The paper presents a new mathematical constant with no immediate connection to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: A Complete Classification Of A Reciprocal Degree-Five Quadrinomial Family Over F_{q^2}
authors: Brian M. Woody
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify a reciprocal degree-five quadrinomial family over the quadratic extension F_{q^2}, where q is an odd prime power. The family has four terms, coefficients in F_q, and a coefficient constraint that makes the induced rational function on the unit circle highly structured. The classification has two sharply different branches. When q is congruent to 1 modulo 4, infinite families occur and are governed by two quadratic-character conditions on the parameter b. When q is congruent to 3 modulo 4, a square-class obstruction converts the problem into a character-sum problem on a conic. A Weil-bound argument eliminates all large fields in this branch, and finite verification leaves only the sporadic fields q = 7, 19, 23. The result is a complete classification of the nondegenerate members of the family for all odd prime powers q.
tldr: This paper classifies a reciprocal degree-five quadrinomial family over finite fields, a topic in pure mathematics with no connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: The paper addresses a classification problem in finite field theory, specifically for a family of polynomials with constraints.
method: The classification uses character sums, Weil bounds, and case analysis based on congruence conditions on q.
result: Complete classification is achieved: infinite families for q ≡ 1 mod 4, and only sporadic fields for q ≡ 3 mod 4.
conclusion: The work is a self-contained mathematical classification with no implications for quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Threshold Phenomena And Bounds In Normalized Remainders Of Degenerate Exponential Functions
authors: Prasanta Kumar Ray Artatrana Suna
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we study a normalized remainder [MATH] for the degenerate exponential [MATH] ([MATH]). We establish an integral representation, an exact monotonicity threshold at [MATH], and rigorous conditions for the local failure of logarithmic convexity at the origin. We then prove a sharp asymptotic result: for every [MATH] in the increasing regime [MATH], the second logarithmic derivative satisfies [MATH] as [MATH], showing that global logarithmic convexity on [MATH] fails throughout this regime. We further give a necessary and sufficient condition for absolute monotonicity, showing it holds only on a countable, measure-zero set of parameters, and we derive explicit two-sided truncation-error bounds that are pointwise sharp at the origin.
tldr: This paper studies the monotonicity and convexity properties of a normalized remainder of degenerate exponential functions, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the analytic properties of a normalized remainder function derived from degenerate exponential functions, which is a purely mathematical problem.
method: The paper uses real analysis techniques such as integral representations, logarithmic derivatives, and monotonicity arguments to derive conditions for convexity and absolute monotonicity.
result: The paper establishes an exact monotonicity threshold, shows failure of global logarithmic convexity in a certain regime, and provides sharp truncation-error bounds.
conclusion: The results are purely mathematical and do not relate to any of the specified research directions in quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: On Mersenne-Bernoulli And Mersenne-Euler Polynomials
authors: Prasanta Kumar Ray Artatrana Suna
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The sequence of Mersenne numbers [MATH] is defined as [MATH] In this study we introduce the Mersenne-Bernoulli and Mersenne-Euler polynomials. Using the generating functions and [MATH]-calculus we find some identities associated with them. Moreover, we define the corresponding matrices with these polynomials, factorise them and find their inverses.
tldr: This paper introduces Mersenne-Bernoulli and Mersenne-Euler polynomials, deriving identities and matrix factorizations using generating functions and q-calculus.
motivation: The study aims to extend classical Bernoulli and Euler polynomials to sequences of Mersenne numbers, exploring new polynomial families and their algebraic properties.
method: The authors define generating functions for the new polynomials and apply q-calculus techniques to derive identities. They also construct associated matrices, factorize them, and compute inverses.
result: Several identities involving Mersenne-Bernoulli and Mersenne-Euler polynomials are obtained, along with matrix factorizations and inverses.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of special functions and combinatorial number theory, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A $3$-adic Recurrence For The Fixed Points Of The Josephus Function $j_4$
authors: Roy Quintero-Contreras Yunier Bello-Cruz
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01270v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the Josephus problem with stepsize four, the participants in a circle are eliminated one by one, every fourth person leaving, until a single survivor remains. A fixed point occurs when the survivor turns out to be the person who began in the last seat. The circle sizes with this property form the sequence 1; 21; 38; 51; 122; 163; 689; 919; 2{,}906; and so on, whose gaps fluctuate erratically. This paper explains the fluctuation and turns it into a recurrence. Between consecutive fixed points, the circle sizes at which the survivor falls exactly one or two seats short of the last one, the near-misses, group into alternating blocks of the two kinds, and the length of every block is the number of times three divides a simple quantity built from the circle size that precedes the block. Iterating these divisibility counts carries each fixed point to the next. Stepsize four is the first case in which two kinds of near-miss coexist, and the alternation they force is what separates it from the solved cases of stepsizes two and three. As a byproduct, the survivor's position for an arbitrary circle size can be computed by walking the near-misses of a single interval, in a number of steps proportional to their count, rather than stepping through every smaller circle as the defining recursion does.
tldr: This paper studies a recurrence for fixed points of the Josephus function with stepsize four, a purely combinatorial number theory problem.
motivation: The Josephus problem is a classic elimination game; understanding fixed points and near-misses for stepsize four reveals a pattern not present in smaller stepsizes.
method: The authors analyze the sequence of circle sizes where the survivor is the last person, identify near-misses, and derive a recurrence based on divisibility by 3.
result: They show that between consecutive fixed points, near-misses group into alternating blocks whose lengths are determined by the 3-adic valuation of a simple quantity, leading to an iterative recurrence.
conclusion: The recurrence allows computing the survivor's position for arbitrary circle sizes more efficiently than the defining recursion.

title: Hybrid Two-Level Transport Method With Solution Decomposition In Macro And Micro Components
authors: Dmitriy Y. Anistratov Caleb A. Shaw
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a new hybrid MC/deterministic method for solving the one-group steady-state Boltzmann transport equation based on decomposition of solution in macro and micro components. The macro component captures the large-scale structure of the solution. It is represented by angular moments of the high-order transport solution. The [MATH] approximation is applied to define the macro component. The first two angular moments are obtained as a solution of hybrid low-order moment equations with exact closures. The equation for the micro component is solved using a MC simulation. The hybrid two-level system of equations for macro and micro components is solved by fixed-point iteration scheme. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate variance reduction of stochastic numerical solution and improvement in computational efficiency.
tldr: This paper presents a hybrid Monte Carlo/deterministic method for solving the Boltzmann transport equation using solution decomposition into macro and micro components.
motivation: To improve computational efficiency and reduce variance in stochastic solutions of the Boltzmann transport equation.
method: The macro component is solved via low-order moment equations with exact closures, while the micro component is solved using Monte Carlo simulation, with fixed-point iteration coupling the two levels.
result: Numerical results demonstrate variance reduction and improved computational efficiency compared to standard methods.
conclusion: The hybrid two-level transport method effectively combines deterministic and stochastic approaches for efficient transport equation solving.

title: Bilinear Control Of Age--space Structured Populations
authors: Louis Shuo Wang Jiguang Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study constrained bilinear optimal control for nonlocal age--space structured population equations with renewal boundary conditions and endogenous surveillance feedback. The control acts as a coefficient in a mixed transport--diffusion equation, while a scalar observable generated by the state enters both the interior dynamics and the renewal law. This produces a nonlinear closed-loop control-to-state map and a feedback-dependent adjoint system. Using a characteristic mild formulation rather than a standard Lions--Magenes argument, we establish closed-loop well-posedness and Frechet differentiability. We then derive the reduced and feedback-corrected adjoint equations. The feedback derivative is identified as a low-rank perturbation [MATH]; in the Volterra-kernel regime, the associated transfer operator is quasinilpotent, yielding an explicit resolvent representation of the adjoint. Finally, we prove first-order optimality conditions and decompose the switching function into reduced and feedback-induced components.
tldr: This paper studies bilinear optimal control of age-space structured population models with feedback, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper aims to solve constrained bilinear optimal control problems for nonlocal age-space structured population equations with renewal boundary conditions and endogenous surveillance feedback.
method: The authors use a characteristic mild formulation instead of standard Lions-Magenes argument to establish well-posedness and Fréchet differentiability, then derive reduced and feedback-corrected adjoint equations.
result: The feedback derivative is identified as a low-rank perturbation, and in the Volterra-kernel regime the transfer operator is quasinilpotent, yielding an explicit resolvent representation of the adjoint.
conclusion: First-order optimality conditions are proved, and the switching function is decomposed into reduced and feedback-induced components.

title: Algebraic Conditions For Second-moment Stability Boundaries Of Linear, Time-invariant Stochastic Delay-differential Equations
authors: Harry Dankowicz Zsolt Iklodi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01374v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For linear, time-invariant stochastic delay-differential equations with a single constant delay and both multiplicative and additive noise, this paper derives optimal semi-analytic algebraic equality conditions that can be used to identify second-moment stability boundaries without the use of problem discretization. Successful validation against Monte Carlo simulations and published results for several low-dimensional models clarifies limitations of stability conditions proposed in the literature and demonstrates considerable savings in computational effort relative to discretization-based approaches. In particular, using the theory derived in this paper, second-moment stability boundaries are shown to be computable using parameter continuation techniques applied to discretization-free equality conditions that scale only with the square of the problem dimension. For the case of one-dimensional stochastic delay-differential equations, in particular, the analysis is entirely closed form with a stability condition expressed entirely in terms of elementary functions. These results are enabled by the derivation of an advection-type boundary-value problem with non-local boundary conditions for a three-variable correlation function followed by a reduction to a delay-differential boundary-value problem for a two-variable correlation function. For the former problem, observations regarding the spectral abscissa of the discretization of the corresponding infinitesimal generator, particularly that second-moment stability is lost when a real eigenvalue passes through the origin, motivate identification of second-moment stability boundaries with a loss of uniqueness of stationary solutions to the latter problem.
tldr: This paper derives algebraic conditions for second-moment stability boundaries of linear stochastic delay-differential equations.
motivation: Stability analysis of stochastic delay-differential equations is important in control theory and applied mathematics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors derive an advection-type boundary-value problem for a three-variable correlation function and reduce it to a delay-differential boundary-value problem, then identify stability boundaries via eigenvalue analysis.
result: Optimal semi-analytic algebraic equality conditions are obtained that scale quadratically with problem dimension, validated against Monte Carlo simulations.
conclusion: The method provides efficient computation of stability boundaries without discretization, but the topic is unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: A Local Macroscopic Conservative (LoMaC) Low Rank Tensor Method For The Vlasov-Maxwell System
authors: Wei Guo Shadi Heenatigala
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The main computational challenges of solving the Vlasov-Maxwell (VM) system include the high dimensionality of the phase space, nonlinearity, inherent conservation properties, among others. In this paper, we develop a novel Local Macroscopic Conservative (LoMaC) low rank tensor method for the VM system, as a continuation of our previous work (arXiv:2207.00518). The method takes advantage of the tensor friendly structure of the Vlasov equation and employs the low rank hierarchical Tucker decomposition to approximate the Vlasov solution in high dimensions. Hence, the curse of dimensionality can be mitigated. Furthermore, to realize the LoMaC property, the algorithm simultaneously evolves the conservation laws of mass, momentum and energy alongside the Vlasov equation using a high order conservative method with the kinetic flux vector splitting. By a conservative orthogonal projection, the low rank solution is guaranteed to have the same macroscopic observables updated from the conservation laws. A collection of numerical tests on the VM system are presented to demonstrate the efficiency and efficacy of the proposed algorithm.
tldr: This paper develops a low rank tensor method for solving the Vlasov-Maxwell system in plasma physics.
motivation: The Vlasov-Maxwell system is high-dimensional and computationally challenging; existing methods struggle with conservation properties and curse of dimensionality.
method: The method uses hierarchical Tucker decomposition to approximate the Vlasov solution and evolves macroscopic conservation laws via a conservative orthogonal projection.
result: Numerical tests demonstrate efficiency and efficacy of the proposed algorithm for the Vlasov-Maxwell system.
conclusion: The LoMaC low rank tensor method provides a promising approach for simulating plasma physics while preserving conservation laws.

title: Delay Effects On The Discontinuous Stabilization Of The Nonholonomic Integrator And Its Generalizations
authors: Anthony Bloch William Clark
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01386v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The nonholonomic integrator is a famous example in feedback design - although it is small-time locally controllable to the origin, no continuous feedback law exists. Therefore, any stabilizing feedback laws must be either time-varying or discontinuous. A previously studied discontinuous feedback law stabilizes initial conditions lying between two paraboloids and has a sliding mode on the [MATH]-plane. We investigate the effect of introducing delays into this discontinuous feedback law. To a first-order analysis, the lag causes the sliding mode of the [MATH]-plane to bifurcate into two switching regions where the resulting dynamics can be interpreted as a hybrid dynamical system with hysteresis. Counterintuitively, the presence of a delay can actually have a positive effect on both the size of the basin of attraction and the convergence rate of the controller. We also consider the natural generalization of the nonholonomic integrator to higher dimensions.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of delays on a discontinuous feedback law for stabilizing the nonholonomic integrator, a control theory problem.
motivation: The nonholonomic integrator is a canonical example in control theory where no continuous feedback stabilizer exists, motivating the study of discontinuous or time-varying laws. Understanding delay effects is crucial for practical implementation.
method: The authors analyze a previously proposed discontinuous feedback law with delays, modeling the resulting dynamics as a hybrid system with hysteresis due to switching regions.
result: Counterintuitively, delays can enlarge the basin of attraction and improve convergence rate. The analysis is extended to higher-dimensional generalizations.
conclusion: Delays can have beneficial effects on stabilization of the nonholonomic integrator, challenging the typical view that delays are detrimental.

title: Fredholm--residue Selection Of The Unsteady Kutta Amplitude
authors: Louis Shuo Wang Jiguang Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an operator-theoretic interpretation of unsteady Kutta selection in trailing-edge acoustic receptivity. The inviscid acoustic--wake problem leaves one outgoing wake amplitude undetermined. We show that, under explicit structural hypotheses, this amplitude is the same scalar obtained from three representations: cancellation of the inverse-square-root edge singularity, Fredholm compatibility of the viscous lower-deck problem, and the residue of the Kutta-normalized transform solution at the downstream wake pole: [MATH]. The inner Fredholm--edge mechanism is verified exactly in a linear-shear lower-deck model, where the primal shear and adjoint velocity are Airy fields and the edge concomitant is nonzero outside a discrete resonance set.
tldr: This paper presents an operator-theoretic interpretation of unsteady Kutta selection in trailing-edge acoustic receptivity, using Fredholm compatibility and residue calculus.
motivation: The unsteady Kutta condition leaves one wake amplitude undetermined; the authors aim to resolve this ambiguity through mathematical consistency conditions.
method: The authors show that the amplitude is determined by three equivalent representations: cancellation of the edge singularity, Fredholm compatibility of the viscous lower-deck problem, and the residue of the Kutta-normalized transform at the downstream wake pole. They verify the mechanism in a linear-shear lower-deck model using Airy fields.
result: The three representations yield the same scalar amplitude, and the inner Fredholm-edge mechanism is verified exactly in the model, with the edge concomitant nonzero outside a discrete resonance set.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous mathematical framework for unsteady Kutta selection, linking edge singularity cancellation to Fredholm theory.

title: Pure Infiniteness And Primary Factorisation
authors: Antonio Acuaviva, Bence Horv\'ath, Tomasz Kania
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01467v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that there is no real or complex indecomposable Banach space with the primary factorisation property (PFP). We relate the PFP of a Banach space [MATH] to ring-theoretic infiniteness of [MATH] and of [MATH], where [MATH] denotes the set of operators not factoring the identity on [MATH], in the case it is the unique maximal ideal of [MATH]. For complex [MATH] with the PFP, this quotient is purely infinite exactly when it is not scalar. We isolate the quantitative gap relevant to ultrapowers, identify classical sequence spaces as positive non-scalar cases, and show that Read's space [MATH] does not have the uniform PFP.
tldr: This paper studies pure infiniteness and primary factorisation in Banach spaces, which is a topic in functional analysis with no connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the structure of indecomposable Banach spaces and the primary factorisation property, a purely mathematical question.
method: The paper uses techniques from Banach space theory and ring theory, analyzing maximal ideals and ultrapowers.
result: It shows that no real or complex indecomposable Banach space has the primary factorisation property, and relates this to ring-theoretic infiniteness.
conclusion: The results are of interest to functional analysts but have no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Boundary-Aware Quantization: Finite-Scale Decision Geometry Of Neural Classifiers
authors: O. M. Kiselev
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We measured quantization-induced decision-boundary changes using local logit-margin radii, first-order boundary displacement, normal variation, slice-boundary Jaccard distance, grid prediction changes, multiclass junction counts, and low-margin boundary-band flips. On the digits benchmark, 8-bit weight quantization preserved all test labels while producing boundary-mask Jaccard \(0.428\) on the PCA slice; at 4 bits, accuracy remained \(0.9733\), while boundary Jaccard rose to \(0.970\) and median local boundary shift reached \(0.0290\). Interpolation between adjacent quantization levels localized the visible reconfigurations at multiclass junctions, with 12, 34, and 17 triple-junction cells in the selected transitions. Calibration-to-test stopping reduced the digits held-out flip rate from \(0.0094\) to \(0.0022\) and boundary Jaccard from \(0.825\) to \(0.524\); the same stopping rule also reduced flips on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST. On official CIFAR-10 subsets, PTQ-W selected by accuracy gave 6-bit flip \(0.0367\) and boundary Jaccard \(0.184\), whereas boundary-aware stopping selected 8-bit flip \(0.0083\) and boundary Jaccard \(0.048\). On full CIFAR-10 with three seeds, 6-bit PTQ-W lost \(0.0029\) accuracy relative to float, changed \(5.3\%\) of held-out decisions, and changed \(24.5\%\) of low-margin boundary-band decisions. A fixed-bit boundary-gap rounding term changed the trade-off at 4 bits by reducing boundary Jaccard from \(0.457\) to \(0.435\) and boundary-band pair-order flip from \(0.3600\) to \(0.3558\), with an accuracy trade-off; the 3-bit stress test exposed the tuning limit of this surrogate. Calibration boundary Jaccard predicted held-out boundary Jaccard across PTQ-W and optimized rounding variants with \(r=0.947\)--\(0.994\).
tldr: This paper studies quantization-induced decision boundary changes in neural classifiers using geometric measures.
motivation: To understand how weight quantization affects the decision geometry of neural networks and to develop boundary-aware quantization methods.
method: The authors introduce local logit-margin radii, boundary displacement, Jaccard distance, and other metrics to quantify boundary changes, and propose a calibration-to-test stopping rule for quantization.
result: 8-bit quantization preserves test labels; boundary-aware stopping reduces flip rates and boundary Jaccard distance; a fixed-bit boundary-gap rounding term improves trade-offs at 4 bits.
conclusion: Boundary-aware metrics can guide quantization to preserve decision boundaries, improving reliability of quantized classifiers.

title: Admission And Assortment Optimization For Multi-size Automated Parcel Lockers
authors: Carlos An\'ibal Su\'arez, Antoine Deza, Tal Raviv
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study admission control and capacity design for automated parcel lockers with multiple parcel and locker sizes. A smaller parcel can use a larger locker, but doing so may block a future larger parcel whose rejection is more costly. We formulate the admission problem as a finite-state, infinite-horizon average-cost Markov decision process and solve small instances exactly by relative value iteration. We analyze the always-accept (AA) policy, which admits every feasible parcel into the remaining compatible capacity, and give a sufficient condition for its optimality. Across two-, three-, and four-size experiments, AA is optimal in fast-pickup regimes and nearly optimal when holding times are longer; observed optimality gaps are negligible even when AA is not optimal. We then study the locker-assortment problem, which minimizes facility cost plus optimal expected rejection cost. We give an exact bound-and-enumerate algorithm for moderate-size instances. Although the objective is not discrete convex, exchange-neighborhood local search finds the certified optimum in every instance for which exact certification is computationally tractable, and it scales as a heuristic to larger systems.
tldr: This paper studies admission control and capacity design for automated parcel lockers with multiple sizes, using Markov decision processes and optimization.
motivation: To optimize the operation and design of automated parcel lockers, which are a practical logistics problem.
method: Formulates the admission problem as a finite-state, infinite-horizon average-cost MDP and solves small instances exactly; analyzes the always-accept policy and gives a sufficient condition for optimality; solves the locker-assortment problem with a bound-and-enumerate algorithm and local search.
result: The always-accept policy is optimal in fast-pickup regimes and nearly optimal otherwise; the local search heuristic finds certified optima for moderate instances.
conclusion: The proposed methods provide efficient solutions for parcel locker management and design.

title: Uniformly Positive Mean Dimension
authors: Elon Lindenstrauss Tal Barak
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01501v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the relation between uniformly positive entropy and uniformly positive mean dimension at the level of fixed open covers. To a symbolic system X, we associate a hub-and-spoke system Spoke(X), obtained by replacing each symbol by a one-dimensional spoke attached to a common hub. We prove that if X admits a shift-invariant measure of full support, then Spoke(X) has completely positive mean dimension. We also prove that if X has uniformly positive entropy, then Spoke(X) has uniformly positive mean dimension. Finally, using symbolic codings of irrational rotations on tori, we construct hub-and-spoke systems with completely positive mean dimension but without uniformly positive mean dimension or uniformly positive entropy. The examples are nondegenerate: the relevant covers have zero mean dimension and zero entropy, but when refined by iterating under the dynamics the corresponding covering numbers are unbounded.
tldr: This paper studies uniformly positive mean dimension in symbolic systems and hub-and-spoke systems, a topic in topological dynamics.
motivation: To understand the relationship between uniformly positive entropy and uniformly positive mean dimension for fixed open covers.
method: Introduces a hub-and-spoke system construction and analyzes its mean dimension and entropy properties using symbolic codings of irrational rotations.
result: Shows that under certain conditions, hub-and-spoke systems can have completely positive mean dimension without uniformly positive mean dimension or entropy.
conclusion: The examples demonstrate that positive mean dimension does not imply uniformly positive mean dimension or entropy, highlighting subtle distinctions in dynamical complexity.

title: Flexible And Reliable Network Design For Emerging Transportation Services: Multi-stage Stochastic Programming Approach
authors: Riki Kawase, Koki Satsukawa, Toru Seo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a general framework for flexible and reliable network design problems (FR-NDPs). The framework enables planners to change infrastructure investments in response to realized uncertainties, while ensuring desired levels of reliability. Motivated by emerging transportation services such as shared autonomous vehicle (SAV) systems, where historical data are scarce and technological developments uncertain, FR-NDPs integrate strategic investment decisions with operational control. We formulate the FR-NDPs as risk-averse multi-stage stochastic problems to be solvable by stochastic dual dynamic programming (SDDP) and establish sufficient conditions under which strategic and operational subproblems converge to the global optimum. We illustrate applications to SAV capacity expansion and integrated SAV-BRT (Bus Rapid Transit) route design, and numerical experiments on a Midtown Manhattan network highlight three key findings: (i) flexibility and reliability act complementarily to hedge against severe scenarios while mitigating the loss of expected performance; (ii) flexibility in investment planning allows dynamic risk hedging, with risk-averse planners reducing early-stage investments to preserve adaptability; and (iii) differences in operational flexibility between SAV and BRT systems are reflected in strategic decisions, with risk-averse planners tending to refrain investment in transport modes with lower operational flexibility.
tldr: This paper proposes a multi-stage stochastic programming framework for flexible and reliable network design in emerging transportation services like shared autonomous vehicles.
motivation: Emerging transportation services face uncertainties due to scarce historical data and uncertain technological developments, requiring flexible and reliable infrastructure investment strategies.
method: The authors formulate the problem as risk-averse multi-stage stochastic programs solved by stochastic dual dynamic programming (SDDP), establishing convergence conditions for strategic and operational subproblems.
result: Numerical experiments on a Manhattan network show that flexibility and reliability complement each other, risk-averse planners reduce early investments to preserve adaptability, and operational flexibility differences affect strategic decisions.
conclusion: The proposed framework effectively integrates flexibility and reliability in network design, providing insights for investment planning under uncertainty.

title: A Spectral-subspace-augmented POD-Galerkin Method For Parametrized PDEs With Limited Snapshot Data
authors: Zecheng Gan Tianhao Hu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parametrized partial differential equations (PDEs) arise in many-query simulation, optimization, control, and uncertainty quantification, where repeated full-order solves restrict the number of high-fidelity snapshots that can be generated. This limitation is particularly pronounced in computational energy science, where multiscale models of porous-media flow, transport, and energy materials often make large snapshot datasets impractical. Proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) constructs compact reduced bases from solution snapshots, but it may exhibit limited out-of-sample predictive capability when the snapshots insufficiently sample the solution manifold. To address this limitation, we propose a spectral-subspace-augmented POD-Galerkin method (SS-POD) tailored to limited-data regimes. SS-POD starts from a problem-adapted spectral approximation space, partitions it into orthogonal subspaces, and performs POD locally on the projected snapshot matrices. An energy-balancing rule determines the spectral partition so that the resulting local POD problems are assigned comparable amounts of snapshot energy. For nonlinear parametrized PDEs, SS-POD is coupled with the discrete empirical interpolation method (DEIM). Numerical experiments show that SS-POD improves out-of-sample accuracy over standard POD-Galerkin while retaining compact reduced bases in limited-snapshot regimes. In particular, for a Laplace-Beltrami problem on the unit sphere with only 5 snapshots, SS-POD achieves a relative error of [MATH] using 91 basis functions, whereas the standard POD error saturates at [MATH] and the spectral-Galerkin method requires 256 basis functions for comparable accuracy. These results indicate that SS-POD provides an effective strategy for high-fidelity reduced-order modeling from limited snapshot data.
tldr: This paper proposes a spectral-subspace-augmented POD-Galerkin method for reduced-order modeling of parametrized PDEs with limited snapshot data.
motivation: Standard POD-Galerkin methods suffer from poor out-of-sample accuracy when only a few high-fidelity snapshots are available, which is common in computational energy science.
method: The method constructs a problem-adapted spectral approximation space, partitions it into orthogonal subspaces, performs local POD on projected snapshot matrices, and uses an energy-balancing rule to determine the partition.
result: Numerical experiments show that SS-POD achieves significantly lower relative errors than standard POD-Galerkin with comparable basis sizes, e.g., on a Laplace-Beltrami problem with only 5 snapshots.
conclusion: SS-POD provides an effective reduced-order modeling strategy for high-fidelity simulations in limited-data regimes.

title: Multi-Domain Matrix Framework For Human Resource Decision Support
authors: Daehan Lee, Jaemyung Ahn, Jaewoo Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents an actionable human resource (HR) decision-support framework for small firms and startups based on a multi-domain matrix (MDM). The framework addresses three key challenges faced by small organizations: complex interdependencies among organizational components; the lack of systematic analytical tools for HR decision-making; and the need for rapid responses in fast-changing organizational environments. The proposed framework formulates startup human resource management as a multi-domain structural modeling problem, where members, skills, and projects are interconnected domains within an integrated MDM. Based on this representation, the framework provides qualitative analysis guidelines and quantitative metrics for diagnosing an organization's HR state and supporting personnel decisions on workload redistribution, hiring, and capability development. A case study of MDM-based HR decisions for an early-stage technology startup is conducted to demonstrate the framework's practical applicability. The application shows that the framework can identify workload imbalances, reveal a key member with an unsustainable workload, and inform a subsequent hiring decision. The framework can be further applied after the hiring of a new member to track changes in the organization's multi-domain structure and support continuous HR diagnosis.
tldr: This paper presents a multi-domain matrix framework for human resource decision support in small firms and startups.
motivation: Small organizations lack systematic analytical tools for HR decision-making and need rapid responses to changing environments.
method: The framework models members, skills, and projects as interconnected domains in a multi-domain matrix, providing qualitative and quantitative metrics for HR diagnosis.
result: A case study on an early-stage startup identifies workload imbalances and informs hiring decisions.
conclusion: The framework can support continuous HR diagnosis and decision-making in small organizations.

title: Post-Processing Reduced-Order Models For Transport-Dominated Problems By Gegenbauer Reconstruction
authors: Lei Yan, Yan Jiang, Chi-Wang Shu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop a physics-based post-processing technique for data-driven reduced-order models (ROMs) of transport-dominated problems. Besides the slow decay of the Kolmogorov n-width, ROMs based on globally supported bases often produce unphysical oscillations when approximating solutions with shocks or sharp gradients, a phenomenon analogous to Gibbs oscillations in spectral approximations. To address this issue, we introduce a post-processing framework based on Gegenbauer polynomial reconstruction. The key idea is to re-project the ROM solution onto a Gegenbauer polynomial basis over each interval of analyticity. Originally developed for spectral approximations, Gegenbauer reconstruction achieves spectral accuracy while effectively suppressing Gibbs oscillations. We extend this technique to data-driven ROMs and consider three representative approaches: Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD)-Galerkin ROM, Operator Inference (OpInf), and nonlinear manifold ROMs based on convolutional autoencoders (CAE). Numerical results show that the proposed post-processing consistently removes spurious oscillations and substantially improves solution quality for all three ROMs. For one-dimensional problems, the method is straightforward to implement once discontinuities are detected. We further develop a practical extension to two-dimensional problems using line-by-line reconstruction in each coordinate direction. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method reduces errors by up to one or two orders of magnitude for inviscid transport problems and significantly outperforms total variation regularization in both numerical accuracy and the sharp resolution of discontinuities.
tldr: This paper develops a post-processing technique using Gegenbauer polynomial reconstruction to suppress Gibbs oscillations in reduced-order models for transport-dominated problems.
motivation: Reduced-order models for transport-dominated problems suffer from unphysical oscillations due to the slow decay of Kolmogorov n-width, analogous to Gibbs oscillations in spectral methods.
method: The authors propose a post-processing framework that re-projects the ROM solution onto a Gegenbauer polynomial basis over intervals of analyticity, extending the technique from spectral approximations to data-driven ROMs including POD-Galerkin, Operator Inference, and convolutional autoencoder-based nonlinear manifolds.
result: Numerical experiments show that the method consistently removes spurious oscillations and reduces errors by up to one or two orders of magnitude for inviscid transport problems, outperforming total variation regularization.
conclusion: Gegenbauer reconstruction is an effective post-processing tool for improving solution quality of ROMs for transport-dominated problems with shocks or sharp gradients.

title: Stream Function -- Pressure Virtual Element Methods For The Stokes--Darcy Interface Problem
authors: Franco Dassi, Rekha Khot, David Mora, Andres E. Rubiano, Ricardo Ruiz-Baier
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces a novel Virtual Element Method (VEM) for the coupled Stokes--Darcy system in primal-primal form. In the free-flow Stokes domain, we implement a stream function formulation that inherently satisfies the incompressibility constraint and reduces computational cost. Across the interface, mass conservation, normal stress balance, and the Beavers--Joseph--Saffman slip condition are enforced to couple the biharmonic stream function equation with the Darcy's pressure equation. Leveraging VEM's ability to handle general polygonal meshes, the proposed method naturally accommodates irregular interface geometries without requiring remeshing or adaptive refinement. The accuracy of the method is validated through several numerical simulations that include applications to dead-end filtration, and network flow in bioartificial organs.
tldr: This paper presents a virtual element method for solving the Stokes-Darcy interface problem using a stream function formulation.
motivation: The Stokes-Darcy problem models coupled free flow and porous media flow, important in applications like filtration and bioartificial organs. Existing methods often struggle with irregular interface geometries.
method: The authors develop a virtual element method (VEM) that uses a stream function formulation in the Stokes domain to enforce incompressibility, and couples it with Darcy's pressure equation across the interface via mass conservation, normal stress balance, and Beavers-Joseph-Saffman slip condition.
result: Numerical simulations validate the method's accuracy for problems including dead-end filtration and network flow in bioartificial organs, demonstrating its ability to handle general polygonal meshes without remeshing.
conclusion: The proposed VEM provides an effective and flexible approach for solving the Stokes-Darcy interface problem on complex geometries.

title: Dynamic Modeling And Parameter Estimation For Origami Structure Reconfiguration Process
authors: Yuto Tanaka, Ran Dai, Mehran Mesbahi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The reconfiguration of origami during the folding and unfolding process is governed through a sequence of panel deformations and hinge orientations. To develop an effective model for representing the reconfiguration process, this paper introduces planar straight-line graphs and a novel consensus protocol for reaching the target origami configuration. The convergence and stability properties of the proposed consensus protocol are subsequently analyzed. Furthermore, to account for aggregate material and structural effects in the proposed consensus-based reconfiguration model, effective parameters embedded in the consensus protocol are identified from trajectory data using a fitting algorithm. Lastly, the effectiveness of the proposed modeling approach is shown using simulations of the two-panel structure and the Kresling origami pattern reconfiguration process.
tldr: This paper models origami structure reconfiguration using consensus protocols and parameter estimation, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To develop an effective model for the folding and unfolding process of origami structures.
method: Introduces planar straight-line graphs and a consensus protocol to reach target configurations, with parameter identification from trajectory data.
result: Simulations of two-panel and Kresling origami patterns demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed modeling approach.
conclusion: The consensus-based model can effectively represent origami reconfiguration dynamics.

title: Decentralized Stochastic Subgradient-type Methods With Communication Compression For Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization
authors: Siyuan Zhang, Nachuan Xiao, Xin Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01755v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider the nonsmooth nonconvex decentralized optimization problem, where inter-agent communication is compressed. We propose a general framework that unifies various decentralized stochastic subgradient-type methods with unbiased compression and contractive compression with error compensation. By relating the consensus-error iterates and the averaged iterates to the trajectories of continuous-time differential inclusions, we establish global convergence for all methods encompassed by our framework when the objective functions are nonsmooth and lack Clarke regularity. Based on our framework, we further develop several compression-based methods, including decentralized stochastic subgradient methods utilizing sign-based regularization and gradient-tracking momentum. Preliminary numerical experiments empirically support our theoretical results and highlight the communication-accuracy trade-off of the newly developed methods.
tldr: This paper proposes a framework for decentralized stochastic subgradient methods with communication compression for nonsmooth nonconvex optimization.
motivation: Decentralized optimization with communication constraints is important for distributed machine learning, but existing methods often assume smoothness or convexity, limiting applicability.
method: The authors unify various decentralized subgradient methods with unbiased and contractive compression, and analyze convergence via continuous-time differential inclusions without requiring Clarke regularity.
result: Global convergence is established for the proposed framework, and new methods like sign-based regularization and gradient-tracking momentum are developed, with numerical experiments showing communication-accuracy trade-offs.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for decentralized nonsmooth nonconvex optimization with compressed communication, but is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: On Super Delta-points And The convex-DLD2P In Absolute Sums
authors: Joanna Markowicz Juan Guerrero-Viu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We partially answer two open questions concerning diameter two properties in absolute sums. First, we identify the conditions that a super [MATH]-point in an absolute sum of Banach spaces imposes on the coordinates. Secondly, we show that the convex diametral local diameter two property (convex-DLD2P) passes from an absolute sum [MATH] to its factors whenever [MATH] is not the [MATH]-norm.
tldr: This paper studies diameter two properties in absolute sums of Banach spaces, which is a topic in functional analysis.
motivation: The authors aim to answer open questions about super delta-points and the convex diametral local diameter two property in absolute sums.
method: They analyze conditions for super delta-points in absolute sums and show that the convex-DLD2P passes from an absolute sum to its factors under certain norm conditions.
result: They partially answer two open questions regarding diameter two properties in absolute sums.
conclusion: The results contribute to the theory of Banach spaces but have no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Variational Nonlocal Phase-Field Model For Dynamic Fracture In Elastic Solids
authors: Qing Cheng, Yuqi Sun, Xuejun Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01881v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a variational nonlocal phase-field model for dynamic fracture in elastic solids. The proposed formulation is distinguished by three main features. First, the model is formulated through nonlocal kinematics and kernel-dependent function spaces, allowing weaker regularity requirements while recovering the classical local theory as the nonlocal interaction domain vanishes. Second, a nonlocal crack-surface functional is introduced as an integral counterpart of the Ambrosio--Tortorelli regularization, so that the characteristic length of the diffusive crack is implicitly determined by the nonlocal interaction domain rather than by a prescribed length scale. Third, the degraded nonlocal elastic energy and the nonlocal crack-surface functional are combined into a variationally consistent dynamic fracture system, consisting of a nonlocal momentum balance and an irreversible nonlocal gradient-flow evolution law for the phase field. The coupled system is solved using two temporal discretization strategies: a structure-preserving scalar auxiliary-variable scheme and a staggered alternating scheme, both combined with finite element discretization in space. Numerical examples involving Mode-I fracture, dynamic crack branching, Kalthoff--Winkler-type shear fracture, and fragmentation show that the proposed model captures complex crack initiation, propagation, branching, and interaction without explicit crack tracking. Quantitatively, the predicted crack-tip velocities remain below [MATH] in the dynamic branching and shear-loading tests, and the shear-loading benchmark gives an inclined crack path of approximately [MATH], consistent with the characteristic Kalthoff--Winkler fracture pattern.
tldr: This paper develops a variational nonlocal phase-field model for dynamic fracture in elastic solids.
motivation: Classical phase-field fracture models rely on local kinematics and a prescribed length scale, which may not capture nonlocal effects and require higher regularity.
method: The model uses nonlocal kinematics and a nonlocal crack-surface functional, combined with a variationally consistent dynamic fracture system solved via structure-preserving and staggered schemes with finite elements.
result: Numerical tests show the model captures complex crack patterns without explicit tracking, and predicted crack-tip velocities and crack angles match known benchmarks.
conclusion: The proposed nonlocal phase-field model effectively simulates dynamic fracture phenomena and recovers classical local theory as the nonlocal interaction domain vanishes.

title: Cognitive Warfare, Hybrid Pressure, And Sovereign Resilience: An Operations Research Framework Applied To The Iranian Case (2017--2026)
authors: Rahimeh Neamatian Monemi, Shahin Gelareh, Nelson Maculan
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01894v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A defending state facing sustained economic, media, and psychological pressure from an adversary that continuously re-optimises its campaign poses a problem that existing attacker-defender models in operations research do not directly resolve, because they treat the defender's state as a discrete allocation rather than a continuous, slow-moving institutional process. We formulate a coupled dynamical system in which grievance and institutional resilience evolve continuously while pressure intensity is chosen by an optimising Markov decision process, prove existence and local stability of the resulting equilibrium, and prove a formal result distinguishing it from standard feedback-stability analysis and from a stationary Markov chain treated in isolation. We validate the framework computationally using thirty randomised network instances, full value iteration, and a documented case study of cognitive warfare directed at Iran (2017--2026). The historically calibrated case sits approximately twenty-five times above the computed operational collapse boundary, and a greedy seeding policy reaches eighty-seven percent average network penetration across the randomised instances, significantly above a degree-centrality baseline. A practitioner can use the equilibrium and boundary computation to assess where a specific case sits relative to collapse, rather than relying on an unverified comparison between opposing pressure intensities.
tldr: This paper applies operations research and dynamical systems to model cognitive warfare and institutional resilience, using Iran as a case study.
motivation: Existing attacker-defender models treat the defender's state as discrete allocations, but real-world institutional resilience evolves continuously under sustained pressure.
method: A coupled dynamical system is formulated where grievance and resilience evolve continuously, and pressure intensity is chosen by an optimizing Markov decision process; existence and stability of equilibrium are proved, and validated with randomized networks and a historical case study.
result: The Iran case sits ~25 times above the computed collapse boundary; a greedy seeding policy achieves 87% average network penetration across randomized instances.
conclusion: The framework allows practitioners to assess a specific case's proximity to collapse, rather than relying on unverified comparisons of pressure intensities.

title: Topologically Free Minimal Actions Without Dynamical Comparison
authors: Akshara Prasad Paolo Boldrini
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show the existence of a topologically free minimal action of [MATH] on the Cantor space that does not have dynamical comparison. Moreover, we show that this phenomenon can happen both in the presence and in the absence of invariant measures. We also show that strict comparison of the reduced crossed product C*-algebra does not imply dynamical comparison for minimal actions. Our technique involves constructing a monoid which is not almost unperforated, embedding it into a countable refinement monoid and then realising it as the type semigroup associated to a dynamical system.
tldr: This paper constructs a topologically free minimal action on the Cantor space that lacks dynamical comparison, and relates this to properties of the reduced crossed product C*-algebra.
motivation: To understand the relationship between dynamical comparison and strict comparison in C*-algebras, and to find counterexamples to the implication that strict comparison implies dynamical comparison.
method: Constructs a monoid that is not almost unperforated, embeds it into a countable refinement monoid, and realizes it as the type semigroup of a dynamical system.
result: Existence of a topologically free minimal action without dynamical comparison, both with and without invariant measures; strict comparison of the reduced crossed product does not imply dynamical comparison.
conclusion: Dynamical comparison is not equivalent to strict comparison for minimal actions, and the type semigroup approach can produce such counterexamples.

title: Transferring Supremum-norm Rates And Weak Convergence Of Covariance Kernel Estimators To Functional Principal Components
authors: Kevin Wilk Hajo Holzmann
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that [MATH]-perturbation theory can be used to transfer rates of convergence in the supremum norm as well as weak convergence in the space of continuous functions from covariance kernel estimators to the associated functional principle components (FPCs). As an application we obtain optimal rates of convergence in sup-norm, including minimax-lower bounds, as well as asymptotic normality for estimating the FPCs in a discrete observational model with errors under fixed, synchronous design. The sparse to dense transition which has previously been observed for mean function and covariance kernel estimators also applies to the FPCs. Surprisingly, eigenvalue estimation exhibits a discretization-dominated regime under sparse designs, too. Our results further apply to estimators of cross-covariance and long-run covariance kernels, as well as to covariance kernels of derivative processes. We also present results of numerical experiments in which we use the Nystr\"om method to compute FPCs and eigenvalues, and give an empirical illustration to series of daily temperature curves.
tldr: This paper develops supremum-norm rates and weak convergence for functional principal components from covariance kernel estimators.
motivation: To establish optimal convergence rates and asymptotic normality for functional principal components in discrete observational models with errors.
method: Uses perturbation theory to transfer rates and weak convergence from covariance kernel estimators to functional principal components, and applies Nyström method for computation.
result: Obtains optimal sup-norm rates, minimax lower bounds, and asymptotic normality for FPCs; identifies a discretization-dominated regime for eigenvalue estimation under sparse designs.
conclusion: The results extend to cross-covariance and long-run covariance kernels, and are illustrated on temperature curve data.

title: Low-regularity Finite Element Elasticity Complexes With Hybridizable Stresses On Tetrahedral Alfeld Splits
authors: Xuehai Huang Johnny Guzm\'an
abstract: ArXiv:2607.01933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finite element elasticity complexes of low regularity are constructed on tetrahedral Alfeld splits. In comparison with existing three-dimensional elasticity complexes on such splits, the complexes constructed here lower both the Sobolev regularity and the polynomial degrees, while ending in a hybridizable [MATH]-conforming symmetric stress space with no vertex degrees of freedom. The construction is obtained from local Bernstein-Gelfand-Gelfand arguments applied to polynomial de Rham complexes on the Alfeld split. Two local polynomial elasticity complexes are proved: an [MATH]-[MATH] complex and a lower-regularity [MATH]-[MATH] complex. Their bubble subcomplexes and dimension formulas are derived. These local exact sequences lead to unisolvent finite elements for the displacement and incompatibility spaces and to global finite element subcomplexes of the corresponding elasticity sequences. In the lowest-order [MATH]-[MATH] finite element complex, the [MATH]-conforming tensor space is piecewise cubic. At the same order, the terminal stress-displacement pair recovers the Johnson-Mercier-K\'{i}ek element, while the construction covers higher-order hybridizable symmetric stresses for all [MATH]. A second family gives a low-regularity [MATH]-[MATH] finite element complex for the standard elasticity sequence for all [MATH]. Commuting interpolation diagrams are established for both global complexes.
tldr: This paper constructs low-regularity finite element elasticity complexes on tetrahedral Alfeld splits, focusing on numerical methods for elasticity problems.
motivation: To develop finite element methods for elasticity that require lower Sobolev regularity and polynomial degrees, improving computational efficiency.
method: Uses local Bernstein-Gelfand-Gelfand arguments applied to polynomial de Rham complexes on Alfeld splits to construct two local polynomial elasticity complexes.
result: Obtains unisolvent finite elements for displacement and incompatibility spaces, and global finite element subcomplexes of elasticity sequences with commuting interpolation diagrams.
conclusion: The constructed complexes lower regularity and polynomial degrees while maintaining exactness, providing a framework for hybridizable symmetric stress elements.

title: Numerical Analysis Of The Biot Equations Coupled To Frictional Contact Mechanics
authors: Marius Nevland, Kundan Kumar, Inga Berre, Jakub Wiktor Both, Eirik Keilegavlen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.02030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a mathematical model of a poro-visco-elastic medium subject to frictional contact with a rigid obstacle, and study its numerical approximation. This model couples the Biot equations and contact conditions in the form of normal compliance and Coulomb friction. The resulting variational problem consists of a linear partial differential equation coupled to a nonlinear variational inequality. We propose and analyze a fully discrete numerical scheme for this problem, using conformal finite elements in space and the implicit Euler method in time. Existence and uniqueness of the discrete solution is established, and stability and a priori error estimates are derived. A numerical experiment is performed in which numerical error estimates are computed and compared to the theoretical results.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical analysis of Biot equations coupled with frictional contact mechanics, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper aims to develop and analyze a numerical scheme for poro-visco-elastic media with frictional contact, a problem in computational mechanics.
method: A fully discrete numerical scheme using conformal finite elements in space and implicit Euler in time is proposed, with existence, uniqueness, stability, and error estimates derived.
result: Theoretical error estimates are validated by a numerical experiment.
conclusion: The proposed scheme is effective for simulating coupled poromechanics and contact problems.

title: Nlf: A Resistor-Network Framework And Linear-Time Solver For Convex Network-Flow Equilibria
authors: Oren E. Livne
abstract: ArXiv:2607.02041v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present NLF (Nonlinear Laplacian Flow), a unified framework and linear-time solver for convex network-flow equilibria. Congestion routing, minimum-delay routing, and maximum flow share one form: the nonlinear graph Laplacian [MATH], where a monotone edge law [MATH] encodes the physics (undirected graphs; directed variants are future work). NLF solves it by a damped chord-Newton iteration whose frozen linearization -- a weighted graph Laplacian -- is inverted by a near-linear Laplacian solver (default: approximate Cholesky, LAMG+ interchangeable). The nonlinear solve costs [MATH]--[MATH] linear Laplacian solves, making the wall-clock empirically [MATH] in the edge count [MATH] (not a proved bound). On single-commodity congestion (BPR cost), NLF converges on all 2,003 SuiteSparse corpus graphs up to [MATH] edges. Against a state-of-the-art interior-point method, NLF is a median [MATH] faster where both converge and [MATH] on poorly-separable graphs where the IPM's direct core is superlinear; against L-BFGS, a median [MATH] faster and the only solver to finish on the 90 hardest instances. A multicommodity extension routes [MATH] commodities through one shared hierarchy at [MATH] per step. The same machinery recovers the exact max-flow as a short sequence of Laplacian solves, with the cut potential as a by-product. Code: [URL].
tldr: This paper presents a framework and linear-time solver for convex network-flow equilibria using nonlinear Laplacian flow.
motivation: Efficiently solving network flow problems like congestion routing and maximum flow is important for many applications, but existing methods can be slow on large graphs.
method: The NLF framework formulates the problem as a nonlinear graph Laplacian and solves it via a damped chord-Newton iteration, where each step inverts a weighted graph Laplacian using a near-linear solver.
result: The solver empirically scales linearly with edge count, converges on all 2,003 SuiteSparse graphs, and is significantly faster than interior-point and L-BFGS methods.
conclusion: NLF provides a unified, efficient approach to convex network-flow equilibria with potential extensions to multicommodity flow and max-flow computation.

title: Lower Bounds For Anytime Acceleration Of Gradient Descent
authors: Chung-En Tsai, Ilyas Fatkhullin, Liang Zhang, Niao He
abstract: ArXiv:2607.02053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent work suggests that the convergence rate of gradient descent (GD) in smooth convex optimization can be significantly improved by employing large stepsizes that may violate the descent property. In particular, if the total number of iterations [MATH] is given, an [MATH] convergence rate can be achieved for both function value and squared gradient norm minimization. On the other hand, in the setting of anytime convergence, where [MATH] is not known in advance, the best known rates of GD are much slower: [MATH] for function value minimization and [MATH] for squared gradient norm minimization. It remains open whether any of these upper bounds can be improved, as they are far from the classical [MATH] lower bound for any first-order method. In this work, we establish two lower bounds on the anytime convergence of GD. We show that no positive stepsize schedule can achieve an [MATH] anytime rate for function value minimization, nor an [MATH] anytime rate for squared gradient norm minimization. The key ingredients of our analysis are novel upper bounds on the number and the magnitude of large stepsizes, derived by analyzing GD on quadratic functions and variants of Huber functions. Our work provides the first lower bounds for the COLT 2024 open problem posed by Kornowski and Shamir regarding the optimal anytime convergence rates of GD.
tldr: This paper establishes lower bounds on the anytime convergence rate of gradient descent for smooth convex optimization, showing that no stepsize schedule can achieve rates faster than O(1/k^{2/3}) for function value or O(1/k^{1/2}) for squared gradient norm.
motivation: The anytime convergence of gradient descent with large stepsizes is poorly understood; existing upper bounds are far from classical lower bounds, and it was unknown whether improvements are possible.
method: The authors derive novel upper bounds on the number and magnitude of large stepsizes by analyzing GD on quadratic functions and variants of Huber functions, then use these to prove lower bounds.
result: They prove that no positive stepsize schedule can achieve an O(1/k^{2/3+ε}) anytime rate for function value nor an O(1/k^{1/2+ε}) anytime rate for squared gradient norm.
conclusion: The work provides the first lower bounds for the COLT 2024 open problem, showing that the known upper bounds for anytime GD are essentially tight.

title: Weighted Derivative Histopolation On Arbitrary Grids: Admissibility And Exact Factorizations
authors: Federico Nudo Allal Guessab
abstract: ArXiv:2607.02105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a weighted derivative histopolation framework on families of intervals. The degrees of freedom consist of one scalar normalization and weighted integral moments of the derivative over a prescribed family of subintervals. We prove that the resulting scheme is unisolvent on [MATH] when the interval family separates polynomials of degree at most [MATH] through weighted moments and the normalization is nonzero on constants. Thus, the derivative moments determine the polynomial up to an additive constant, and the scalar normalization fixes this remaining degree of freedom. This gives a sharp criterion for the well-posedness of the interpolation problem and a complete characterization of the admissible scalar normalizations. We then show how admissible families of intervals can be constructed from a fixed grid. When the endpoints of the intervals belong to the grid, admissibility is reduced to the nonsingularity of an interval matrix associated with the family, which depends only on the representation of the intervals in terms of consecutive cells. For Jacobi weights, the associated data matrices have a natural block structure in Jacobi polynomial bases, and the reduced derivative matrix can be expressed in terms of shifted Jacobi moment matrices. We next study Chebyshev configurations in which this structure becomes explicit. For the four classical Chebyshev families, suitable polynomial bases lead to diagonal Gram matrices for the reduced derivative matrices. We show that this diagonal structure depends on the simultaneous choice of the weight, the basis, and the grid. Numerical experiments on equispaced and Chebyshev--Lobatto nodes show the behaviour of the method for different interval families and for different Jacobi parameters.
tldr: This paper introduces a weighted derivative histopolation framework on arbitrary grids, focusing on admissibility and exact factorizations.
motivation: The authors aim to develop a general framework for derivative histopolation that works on arbitrary grids and provides sharp criteria for well-posedness.
method: They define a unisolvent scheme using weighted integral moments of the derivative and a scalar normalization, and analyze admissibility conditions via interval matrices and polynomial bases.
result: They prove that the scheme is unisolvent when the interval family separates polynomials and the normalization is nonzero on constants, and show explicit diagonal structures for Chebyshev configurations.
conclusion: The framework provides a complete characterization of admissible scalar normalizations and demonstrates practical behavior on equispaced and Chebyshev-Lobatto nodes.

title: Universal Minimal Flows Of The Homeomorphism Groups Of Pseudo-solenoids Are Non-metrizable
authors: Aleksandra Kwiatkowska Jan Boronski
